"It's not efficiency or flair that moves people. It's trust." | Lessons to make your company 1% better #020
"It's not efficiency or flair that moves people. It's trust."
No matter how logical your explanation or how attractive your presentation, people will not truly take a step forward unless you have built up a foundation of daily sincerity.

"This approach is more efficient and rational." "Doing this will improve the company's performance." You pitch a new proposal to those around you with perfectly crafted slides and enthusiastic words. Even though they nod and agree that "what you're saying is correct," when it comes time to execute, no one moves, and you end up spinning your wheels alone.

People cannot be moved to action by the content of a proposal alone, no matter how correct or flashy it may be. Following someone's instructions means sharing the risk of responsibility and effort if things go wrong.
It is similar to deciding whether or not to cross a suspension bridge over a deep valley.

No matter how eloquently you explain that "there is a wonderful treasure on the other side" or "you'll save half the time if you cross," if the boards underfoot creak and the wires look rusted, anyone would be too scared to take a single step.
